COMMON QUESTIONS

DayFinder FAQs

Clear answers about accuracy, privacy, holidays and offline use.

Which calendar does DayFinder use?

It uses the proleptic Gregorian calendar from 1583 onward. It does not convert dates from the Julian, Hindu, Islamic or other calendars.

Are Indian holidays complete?

No. The Working Days Calculator includes three national fixed-date references and a small selection of state fixed-date references. Festival, bank and gazette holidays change by year and location, so add the official dates manually.

Can I use the results for legal or payroll decisions?

Use DayFinder as a planning aid, then verify critical results against your organisation’s policy, contract and the relevant official calendar.

Does DayFinder upload my dates?

No. Calculations run in your browser and DayFinder does not require an account. Avoid entering personal information beyond the dates needed for a calculation.

Does it work offline?

After one successful online visit, supported browsers can cache the app for offline use. External Avyuha and GitHub links still require internet access.

Why can historical results differ from old records?

Regions adopted the Gregorian calendar at different times. Old documents may use a local or Julian calendar, while DayFinder applies Gregorian rules consistently.
